extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, policymakers, and the British public concerned with East India Company governance and Indian territories
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary/legislative speech critiquing British ministerial policy toward the Carnatic and Tanjore, arguing principles for just governance, debt treatment, and post-war restoration in Indian territories. It sets out prescriptive standards for what a virtuous ministry ought to do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize population recovery over immediate revenue extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: In order that the people, after a long period of vexation and plunder, may be in a condition to maintain government, government must begin by maintaining them. Here the road to economy lies not through receipt, but through expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minister should invest in restoring the population and productive capacity before attempting to extract revenues; rapid extraction from a devastated country is unjust and counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate funds to restoration rather than debt payments
rubrics_metrics.description: A virtuous and enlightened ministry would have reduced all their most necessary establishments; they would have suspended the justest payments; they would have employed every shilling derived from the producing to reanimate the powers of the unproductive parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporarily reduce governmental costs and redirect available local revenues to repair infrastructure, restart cultivation, and support subsistence rather than servicing private or consolidated debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and repair irrigation reservoirs and waterworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carnatic's rice production depends on reservoirs and watercourses; many reservoirs have been destroyed or fallen into decay and require serious attention and much cost to reëstablish them as means of present subsistence and future revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize irrigation infrastructure as the country’s 'national bank'—prioritize their repair and maintenance as foundational to economic recovery and future revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base decisions on complete, up-to-date information; avoid suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers have wilfully and corruptly suppressed information which they ought to have produced, ignoring committee reports that overturn speculative estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-makers must use and publish accurate, recent reports (not only favorable historical speculations) and must not ignore or suppress official evidence that contradicts their chosen policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use realistic post-war revenue estimates, not speculative peace projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Lord Macartney's 1781 estimate assumes the country restored to ancient prosperity; ministers used such speculative figures rather than the actual, recent receipts and committee accounts showing far lower revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting levies or establishing funds, base calculations on current net receipts and realistic recovery timelines rather than optimistic, restored-peacetime conjectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition territorial assignments to protect natives and ensure management
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers delivered territories back without condition, arrangement, or stipulation of any sort for the natives of any rank, surrendering jurisdiction and revenues to mismanagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers of jurisdiction or revenue should include explicit protections, conditions, and management guarantees to safeguard inhabitants and public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize public defence, civil administration, and investment over private creditor claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference given to private claims over the Company's debt and over funds needed for standing defence and civil government robs the public; public demands supersede private claims by reason of their nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public necessities (army, civil administration, infrastructure) must take precedence over private creditor payments when resources are scarce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating the Company's own territories as indebted to the Company
rubrics_metrics.description: To say that the territory charged with the debt is their own and that their revenues owe them money is to say they are in debt to themselves—nonsense; the Company has merely lost expected incomes due to invasion and ruin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not convert loss of revenue caused by war or devastation into a legal 'debt' the territory must repay to the Company as if the Company were an external creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent high-interest private loans by using direct Company credit or assignments at fair rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of taking direct assignments or lending at the Company’s usual rate (eight percent), the Nabob is driven to borrow from soucars and private assignees at 24–48% compound interest for the benefit of Company servants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funds are needed to service arrears, the Company should lend directly or take direct assignment on fair interest terms rather than permitting private intermediaries to extract ruinous usury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure policy coherence: do not forbid private debts while enabling them
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers renew the old order against contracting private debts yet simultaneously give directions that facilitate contracting such debts (ordering security to soucars who are creditors themselves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws and administrative orders should not reward breaches of prior rules; enforcement and prohibitions must be consistent with enacted administrative practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest and self-securitization in debt arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'soucars' who become security for payment are often the creditors themselves—ministers authorize security on revenues in favor of creditors who then obtain mortgaged territory to secure their own claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debt arrangements should prevent creditors from acting simultaneously as guarantors or security-takers for their own claims; guard against self-dealing that increases charges on the territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit oppressive compound interest and usurious terms on territorial debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Private loans and mortgages have been contracted at 24, 36, and even 48 percent, often with compound interest, producing ruinous burdens on territories like Tanjore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbear schemes that impose extremely high or compound rates; such terms are destructive to the economy and to subjects’ welfare and should be disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect cultivators and local farmers from successive exploitative claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: The European assignee supersedes native farmers, who are then repeatedly replaced and exposed to escalating exactions; cultivators are lashed from oppressor to oppressor, left with barely a grain of corn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative arrangements must prevent a revolving cycle where cultivators suffer from competing claimants; protect local tenants and farmers from being stripped by serial assignees or usurers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not surrender territorial jurisdiction without safeguards for inhabitants
rubrics_metrics.description: The ministers delivered over revenues and territorial jurisdiction to the Nabob without conditions and declared they would never interfere with internal government—leaving inhabitants exposed to plunder and oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrendering jurisdiction should be contingent on agreements that protect inhabitants’ rights and security; abdication of oversight without safeguards is irresponsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid indefinite confiscation of revenues as a war penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: A clause subjects a prince to confiscation of all revenues if the Company becomes involved in war; the confiscation is to remain until every debt the Company 'thinks fit' is discharged—effectively forever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties tied to war-related costs should not amount to perpetual confiscation of a people’s revenues; any wartime levy must be proportionate and time-limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge that country recovery requires time and investment, not instant revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who say the Carnatic will soon recover and become instantly as prosperous as ever are talking nonsense; population, capital, habitation, and infrastructure must be provided in advance and recovery will require expense and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should plan for long-term restoration (capital, seed, stock, irrigation) and not assume immediate return to pre-war productivity; financial planning must reflect realistic recovery horizons.
